The bead-to-PR binding was unauthenticated free text, so any agent permitted to comment on a bead could retire untouched work by appending one 'PR #N opened' line; added owns() requiring headRefName bead/<id> or a '<id>:' title prefix.

The bead's defect recurred during this session (spot-7lj and spot-4gd closed 2026-09-04 on merges into fleet/builder-permissions and bead/spot-2ig) and nothing revisits closed beads; added --audit, and escalated the fleet-side closer fw-y1y which this repo cannot reach.

RELEASED_REF was the bare refname 'origin/main', which gitrevisions resolves as a tag or local branch ahead of the remote-tracking ref, so a pushed tag could choose what counts as shipped; now refs/remotes/origin/main.

verdict_for returned on the first non-merged PR, so a bead naming a superseded PR plus a genuinely stranded one held silently with no note forever; every PR is now judged before a verdict is returned and a strand outranks a hold.

Two lenses flagged that skip and hold verdicts produced no row and no counter, so the summary read '13 beads, 0 closed, 0 stranded, 1 in flight' with twelve unaccounted; every bead now lands under exactly one heading and the counts add up.

PR titles and branch names, author-controlled and editable after merge, were written verbatim into bead close reasons and the run log other agents read; _flatten now strips non-printables, collapses to one line and caps length.

The stranded note's only stated remedy was 'until that branch merges forward', an action ADR 0003 reserves to the human, addressed to whichever unattended agent read it; reworded to name the human as the merge authority.

bead_id reached bd's argv in flag position with no separator, and bd close with no positional id closes the last touched issue, so a dash-leading id could force-close an unrelated bead; calls are now 'bd close --reason X -- id' and 'bd note -- id text'.

'Stranded' was encoded as 'a hold that happens to carry a note' and decoded in two separate places, so attaching an informational note to an ordinary hold would silently reclassify the bead and flip the exit code; added an explicit 'strand' action.

Two lenses flagged that a missing gh binary, a KeyError on renamed gh JSON, or unparseable bd output aborted the whole run with a traceback and discarded the report of closes already applied; _run now returns 127 on FileNotFoundError and the JSON paths are guarded.

The 'merge commit is not in this clone' hold emitted nothing at all and was counted alongside genuinely open PRs, so a bead whose merge commit was pruned would read as in flight indefinitely; hold reasons are now printed under their own heading.

A failing bd note put the same bead under both STRANDED and FAILED and returned 2, obscuring that the strand itself was correctly detected; the strand is now recorded first and the note failure reports as a note failure.

Every subprocess resolved its target from an ambient cwd, so a runner started in the wrong directory would reconcile this board against another repository's pull requests; _run now pins cwd to the repo root.

bd stderr was embedded verbatim in exceptions that reach the run log, and .beads/config.yaml documents github.token and linear.api_key as storable there, so an auth failure could log credential-bearing text; stderr is now flattened and capped.

Comments justified behaviour by 'this runs on a schedule' when nothing schedules it, and a hand-run 'make reconcile-board' died with a bare Error 1 that read as a broken target; comments reworded and the exit code is now explained on its own line.
GH_FIELDS was a single-use constant 120 lines from its only reference; inlined next to the PullRequest construction that consumes it, where anyone adding a field will see it.
The clone() test helper hoisted one set but rebuilt set(reaches) on every call; both are now hoisted so the two lookups read as the same kind of thing.

REJECTED: --released-ref called speculative because no caller varies it. Kept — the bead is precisely about 'released branch' being a stated decision rather than an assumption, and the value is now a fully qualified ref that needs documenting somewhere the operator can see.

REJECTED: --no-fetch called dead configuration. Kept — a git fetch against an unreachable remote blocks on network timeouts rather than failing fast, so an operator needs a way to skip it; I used it myself while verifying offline.
REJECTED: main(argv) takes a parameter no caller supplies. Kept — it is the conventional argparse idiom and it is what makes the CLI callable from a test without patching sys.argv.

REJECTED: reconcile() is a one-line comprehension with a single production caller. Kept — the lens rebutted itself; the test file pairs it with apply_verdicts at nine call sites, so it buys real brevity rather than being speculative.

REJECTED: the new scripts job is 10 lines of scaffolding that could be one step appended to the lint job. Kept — folding it in would gate the scripts tests behind check-claims and behind syncing all five venvs, so a scripts-only failure would surface later and less clearly.

REJECTED: $(ARGS) is interpolated unquoted into the reconcile-board recipe. Kept — ARGS is typed by an operator who already has a shell; the defect would be a scheduler templating ARGS from board or PR data, which nothing does.

REJECTED: pip install uv is unpinned in the new job. Kept — it matches the two pre-existing jobs verbatim; pinning one of three would leave the exposure and add inconsistency, so this belongs in a repo-wide bead not this one.
